item.title: We've tried lyrics, but...
item.content:encoded:
What happens if we were to let SCP-423 interact with an actual score of sheet music? I'm curious to see what would happen if we were to be exposed to something like Prokofiev's "Peter and the Wolf" (is there a new animal character? Is more music written? Does he watch an event transpire, and it's mentioned by the narrator?) or even Shostakovich's 10th Symphony.

Specifically with the Shostakovich, I'm curious to see if SCP-423 would pull something similar with Vonnegut and the Slaughterhouse Five test, where instead of Shostakovich signing his name at rehearsal 164 (D-S-C-H), the instruments instead are rewritten to play F-R-E-D, R being Re. Shostakovich is technically not a "main character," but does insert himself into the music. I'm interested to see if SCP-423 would recognize this fact and consider it "out of the way" enough to rewrite himself in. If SCP-423 is knowledgeable enough to write in new languages (both natural and in coding), could it grasp the fundamentals of music enough to write and rewrite accordingly?

Curious to hear your thoughts, Dr. Mann.

item.title: Entry idea, need word of god on result
item.content:encoded:
Hey, Dr. Mann, I have an idea for a test, but I need you to decide what the result would be.

I know of this web comic where the characters are anthropomorphic animals, but the dialogue never references, or even implies their species. The only way anyone could know they're animals is by seeing the art. So I wondered, if 423 was put into that comic, would he be able to "sense" the illustrations, or would he come out thinking everyone in there was human?

item.title: The Possibilities
item.content:encoded:
I'm terrified to think of what would happen if Fred entered a document describing 2521 (●●|●●●●●|●●|●).
Best case scenario, 2521 rejects it because the paper isn't entirely devoted to it. Worst case scenario, 2521 incorporates Fred into its self-description, and the name Fred becomes a trigger.

This is never going to happen.
So, onto my real question:

How does 423 interact with black boxes and other redactions in text? Fred lives through the narrative; but does he need to see the physical words to understand what was meant? This would explore his relationship with context and ideas not explicitly spelled out in ink, and open up the possibility of Fred decoding confidential papers for the Foundation.

Basically, I want to see Agent Fred make a cameo appearance on a heavily-redacted government file.

item.title: This would be something interesting to post but meh...
item.content:encoded:
Date: ██/██/████
Test Material: SCP-1230

Results: Approximately 15 seconds after manifesting in SCP-1230, SCP-423 re-manifested in the journal, stating that there was “nothing there”.

SCP-1230-1 was later questioned about the experiment, and said that he had “sensed an interloper in [his] pages”. When informed about SCP-423 and his abilities, SCP-1230-1 expressed mild interest in having SCP-423 return once a reader was present.

SCP-423 was informed of the interaction, as well as the abilities of SCP-1230 and SCP-1230-1, the following day. He expressed great interest in visiting when he could. The request was approved, and Dr. D████ was assigned to host the interaction.

For the experiment, the communication journal was placed next to SCP-1230. Dr. D████ read SCP-1230 and went to sleep as normal.

Throughout the resulting dream, Dr. D████ was accompanied by a tall, grey, totally featureless individual named Fred. Upon Dr. D████’s awakening, SCP-423 re-manifested in the journal, expressing extreme satisfaction with the experiment and wishing to do it again as soon as possible.

Notes: SCP-423 is capable of interacting with other text-based sentient entities. SCP-1230 may be used as a future reward for good behavior.

I'm wondering what would happen if you copied a text that already contained 423. Get him into a text, then run that text through a photocopier. Would the copy retain anomalous properties? I imagine it wouldn't because 423 is mostly independent from the actual paper and text itself.
The more interesting test would be what would happen if you got 423 to enter that copy. Would the story then contain two identical characters, the one from the copy and actually 423? That would be similar to the Harry Potter example, but I wonder how he would react to having another version of himself running around in the story.
Or would he simply take on the role of copy!Fred, leaving the copy with one Fred character similar to the test where the experiment log got exposed to him?
